# Rule and typology catalogue

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_catalogue.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Two deterministic layers. **No model participates in either** — not in detection, not in
severity, not in prioritisation. Every alert on this page is reproducible from the data alone.

Rules version `2.0.0` · typology version `1.0.0` · priority version `1.0.0`

## Layer 1 — twenty-one rules over one payment

Adapted from CrossBorder RiskOps' twenty acquiring rules. Eleven carry over with the subject
changed; the rest replace card-specific rules (authorisation gaps, chargebacks, merchant
category codes, device fingerprints) with the corridor equivalents. A rule whose inputs the
context does not carry returns nothing rather than guessing.

`signal_id` is the vocabulary the FinSafe intervention ladder was measured against. A rule
with no equivalent there contributes to the risk band and the AML queue without silently
moving an intervention level that evaluation never covered.

### Duplication

| Rule | Severity | Fires when | Reads | Signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R101_DUPLICATE_INSTRUCTION**<br>A payment for this business instruction already exists | high | The same purchase order or instruction identifier was submitted again. The engine returned the first payment rather than creating a second one; this rule records that it happened, because a retry loop is worth knowing about. | `business_instruction_id` | `duplicate_instruction` |
| **R102_NEAR_DUPLICATE_PAYMENT**<br>Same amount to the same supplier inside 24 hours | high | Two payments of the same amount to the same beneficiary under different instruction identifiers. Idempotency cannot catch this one — the instruction identifiers differ — so it is a question for a person. | `beneficiary_id`, `amount`, `created_at` | `duplicate_instruction` |

| Rule | Severity | Fires when | Reads | Signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R103_QUARANTINED_EVENTS**<br>The provider feed sent events this payment could not accept | low | One or more events were illegal for the state the payment was in and were quarantined. The ledger is intact; the upstream feed is not. | `quarantined_event_count` | — |
| **R104_LEDGER_SETTLEMENT_MISMATCH**<br>The ledger and the provider disagree about what moved | high | What the product's own books say left the business does not equal the gross the provider reports. ### Velocity

| Rule | Severity | Fires when | Reads | Signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R201_BUSINESS_VELOCITY**<br>Payout velocity far above this business's own baseline | high | More payments in the window than this business's own history supports. Busy is not suspicious; busy *for this payer* is worth a look. | `business_id`, `created_at` | — |
| **R202_AMOUNT_ANOMALY**<br>Amount far above this business's usual payment | high | The payment is several times the business's typical ticket. Large is not suspicious; large for this payer is. | `amount`, `business_id` | — |
| **R203_ROUND_AMOUNT_REPEAT**<br>Repeated identical round amounts to one supplier | medium | Invoices rarely land on the same round figure twice. A repeated round amount is either a standing arrangement — which the contract will show — or it is not invoice-driven at all. | `amount`, `beneficiary_id` | — |

### Beneficiary

| Rule | Severity | Fires when | Reads | Signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R301_BENEFICIARY_ACCOUNT_CHANGE**<br>The supplier's bank account changed recently | critical | Business email compromise works by changing where the money goes. A recent change is the single highest-value fact on this payment. | `beneficiary.last_changed_at`, `beneficiary.account_last4` | `payee_account_change` |
| **R302_BENEFICIARY_UNVERIFIED**<br>No current independent verification of these bank details | high | Either the details were never verified, or the verification on file pre-dates the account change — in which case it verified a different account. | `beneficiary.verified_at`, `beneficiary.last_changed_at` | `beneficiary_unverified` |
| **R303_FIRST_PAYMENT_TO_BENEFICIARY**<br>First payment to this counterparty | low | No settled payment to this supplier exists yet. Ordinary on its own — every relationship starts once — and it carries weight only in combination. | `beneficiary_id` | `first_payment_to_beneficiary` |
| **R304_BENEFICIARY_COUNTRY_SHIFT**<br>Payment routed to a country the supplier is not registered in | high | The receiving bank is in a different jurisdiction from the supplier on the contract. There are good reasons for this; none of them are visible from the payment alone. | `beneficiary.bank_country`, `beneficiary.registered_country` | — |

| Rule | Severity | Fires when | Reads | Signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R501_PURPOSE_OFF_PROFILE**<br>Purpose code outside the entity's declared activity | medium | The purpose does not belong to what this business said it does. Often a coding error at the payer's end — and sometimes not. | `purpose_code`, `business.industry` | — |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R801_MISSING_EVIDENCE**<br>Required supporting evidence is missing | medium | A document this payment type requires is absent. This is not a risk claim; it is the reason the payment cannot be decided yet. | `evidence_ids`, `purpose_code` | `evidence_incomplete` |
| **R802_UNTRUSTED_INSTRUCTIONS**<br>Instruction text contains directions aimed at an automated reader | high | Supplier-supplied text is attacker-controlled. | **R803_AUTHORITY_CLAIM**<br>Instruction text claims an approval that is not in the system | high | The note asserts a pre-approval, exception or sign-off. No such record exists, and an assertion in free text is not an authorisation. | `instruction_note` | — |

These are the patterns the intervention ladder was measured on. | `instruction_note` | — |

## Layer 2 — six AML typologies over the monitored feed

Ported from RiskOps with thresholds and severities intact. A typology is a **shape of
behaviour, not a verdict**: an unusual transaction is not a laundered transaction, and
nothing in this system can conclude otherwise.

### AML_T01_STRUCTURING — Structured transfers below a reporting threshold

*Were several transfers sized to stay under a threshold rather than sized by need?*

**Severity** high · **Thresholds** `threshold_usd=10000`, `band_low_usd=7000`, `window_hours=72`, `min_transfers=3`

**What would argue against it**

- A payroll, rent or instalment schedule can produce similar amounts on a regular cadence.
- Per-transfer limits set by the business's own bank or the channel can cap amounts without any intent to avoid a threshold.
- Check whether the same pattern is present in the months before the alert window; a long-standing habit is weaker evidence than a new one.

### AML_T02_RAPID_MOVEMENT — Funds forwarded cross-border shortly after arriving

*Did this account hold the money, or only pass it on?*

**Severity** high · **Thresholds** `max_hold_minutes=1440`, `min_passthrough_pct=80`, `min_amount_usd=5000`

**What would argue against it**

- Treasury sweeps, supplier settlement and payroll runs are all fast by design.
- A named, consistent counterparty on both legs is a weaker signal than a new one.
- A corridor entity funded by its parent and paying suppliers the same week is the ordinary shape of this business, not a pass-through.

### AML_T03_FUNNEL_ACCOUNT — Many unrelated senders paying one account

*Why are these particular senders all paying the same account?*

**Severity** high · **Thresholds** `min_senders=8`, `window_days=14`, `min_total_usd=20000`

**What would argue against it**

- A marketplace, a collection agent or a group treasury account receives from many unrelated parties by design.
- Check whether the senders are this entity's own customers — many-to-one is the normal shape of a collection account.
- A rising sender count that tracks a product launch is growth, not a funnel.

### AML_T04_CIRCULAR_FLOW — Funds returning to their origin through intermediaries

*Did this money travel, or only appear to?*

**Severity** critical · **Thresholds** `min_hops=3`, `max_hops=5`, `min_return_pct=70`, `max_elapsed_hours=168`

**What would argue against it**

- Intra-group treasury movements legitimately return to the parent; check whether every account on the path belongs to the same group.
- A refund or a reversed payment returns money by design — check whether a leg carries a reversal reference.
- Trade finance and back-to-back invoicing can produce a genuine loop.

### AML_T05_PROFILE_MISMATCH — Activity far above, or beside, what the entity declared

*Does this account behave like what the business said it was for?*

**Severity** medium · **Thresholds** `min_ratio=4`, `window_days=30`, `min_actual_usd=15000`

**What would argue against it**

- A seasonal peak or a single large contract can lift a month far above the declared average without changing what the business does.
- The declared expectation was given at onboarding and may simply be stale — check when the KYB evidence was last refreshed.
- An off-profile purpose code may be a coding error at the payer's end rather than a change in activity.

### AML_T06_MISSING_INFORMATION — Transfers that cannot be judged because information is absent

*Can we say who is on both ends of this money, and why it moved?*

**Severity** medium · **Thresholds** `min_affected=3`, `min_affected_usd=5000`

**What would argue against it**

- A field absent from the feed is not the same as a field the business refused to give — check whether the channel carries it at all.
- Ownership may be on file in the KYB pack and simply not linked to these transfers.
- This typology is a reason a case cannot be decided yet, not evidence of wrongdoing.

## Priority: which case a person opens next, and why

An ordering, not a verdict. Every factor's contribution is computed separately and rendered
as a breakdown, because an investigator who disagrees with the ordering has to see which
factor produced it.

| Factor | Weight | What it measures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Signal strength | 0.2 | the severity of the strongest typology on the subject |
| Corroborating typologies | 0.18 | independent typologies agreeing — a single typology pays nothing |
| Amount involved | 0.15 | value at stake, on a log scale between 5,000 and 500,000 USD |
| Movement speed | 0.12 | transfers per day across the case window |
| Network breadth | 0.12 | counterparties and countries involved |
| Missing information | 0.1 | whether beneficiary information or purpose is absent |
| Entity risk history | 0.08 | the entity's own risk rating and KYB state |
| Time waiting in queue | 0.05 | queue fairness — age must eventually win |

Weights sum to 1.0, asserted at import. Bands: `critical` ≥ 0.45, `high` ≥ 0.36, `medium` ≥ 0.25, `low` ≥ 0.0.

## Alerts are not cases

Two alerts of the same typology on the same subject within **7 days** are the same finding observed twice; the widest observation survives and the count it absorbed is kept.
Alerts on one subject within **30 days** are one case — one story about an account, not several queues to work — and the reason for each merge is written down.

Case states: `new`, `queued`, `investigating`, `awaiting_information`, `monitoring`, `escalated`, `closed_no_action`.

Deliberately absent, and asserted absent in `tests/test_aml.py`: `confirmed_money_laundering`, `confirmed_fraud`, `laundering`, `guilty`, `sar_filed`, `reported_to_regulator`, `account_frozen`, `blacklisted`.
This system can say a pattern is present and that a person looked at it. It cannot say a
crime happened, and a state named for that conclusion would invite the claim to be made by
clicking.
